parameters.name: property_type

**Main property use.** Optional  -  but **omitting it is not "both"**: an omitted
`property_type` returns the **residential** plane only.

- `residential`  -  homes and residential land. Same result set as omitting the parameter.

covering both means two calls: one with `commercial` and one without it. The commercial plane
is much the smaller of the two  -  a query that omits `property_type` therefore looks complete
while silently excluding it.

`category` (see its description for how it interacts with `estimatedCount`).

parameters.name: category
parameters.description:
**Property category  -  apartment, villa, land and so on.** Optional. Comma-separated;
several values widen the search (union).

These are the slugs listings actually carry:

- Residential  -  `apartment` · `villa-townhouse` · `floor` · `residential-land` · `land` ·
  `building` · `building-1` · `tower` · `rest-house` · `room` · `hotel`
- Commercial  -  `showroom-1` · `office-space` · `warehouse` · `repair-shop` · `station` ·
  `commercial-rest-house`. Reach these by pairing `category` with `property_type=commercial`.

**Two names are not what you would guess.** Townhouses and villas share one slug,
`villa-townhouse`, and showrooms are `showroom-1` with the numeric suffix. The property-type
taxonomy at `/taxonomy` spells four of these differently, so those spellings are accepted and
normalised for you rather than quietly matching nothing: `villa` → `villa-townhouse`,
`showroom` → `showroom-1`, and `residential-building` / `commercial-building` → `building`
(listings use one merged building slug). The remaining `/taxonomy` spellings are accepted as
written; they select any listing carrying them.

**How this filter behaves.** `category` filters the results on each page. `estimatedCount` is
not category-scoped  -  never quote it as a category total  -  and a page may return fewer rows,
or none, while later pages still match. Page until `hasMore` is `false` rather than stopping
on a short page.

Every returned listing carries its own `category`, so you can always verify the cut.

parameters.name: rega_verified
parameters.description:
**REGA-licensed listings only.** Optional. Filters on the Saudi Real Estate General
Authority advertising licence  -  the regulator's own compliance marker.

- `true`  -  licensed listings only
- `false`  -  the unlicensed remainder

Most of the Saudi catalogue is licensed, so `true` is a light filter and `false` is the interesting
one: it isolates the inventory that has not been through REGA registration, and it is a real
filter rather than a synonym for omitting the parameter.

Every listing also returns its licence data regardless of this filter: `isRegaLicensed`,
`regaLicenceNumber` (the REGA advertising licence number) and `regaFullReference`. Those are
the join keys for cross-referencing against REGA's own records.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
**Page number, 1-indexed.** Optional  -  default `1`, maximum `3000`.

**16 results per page, fixed**  -  there is no page-size parameter; page 2 returns
results 17 - 32. Consecutive pages are disjoint, so paging never
repeats a result.

**Do not page against `estimatedCount`.** On a narrow slice the count over-reports how many
listings are actually retrievable, and on others it is exact  -  you cannot tell which case you
are in up front, so page until `hasMore` comes back `false` instead. `hasMore` is accurate in
both directions: the page after the last populated one is genuinely empty.

The ceiling is the real depth of the catalogue, not a throttle  -  a broad sweep exhausts before
reaching it, and every page up to that point is disjoint from every other, so the catalogue
enumerates without duplicates. Filtered slices run out far sooner. To reach past the ceiling on
a broad query, narrow it and walk each slice  -  by `city_id`, then `zone_id`, then
`neighbourhood_ids`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description:
**Property category  -  apartment, villa, land and so on.** Optional. Comma-separated;
several values widen the search (union).

These are the slugs listings actually carry:

- Residential  -  `apartment` · `villa-townhouse` · `floor` · `residential-land` · `land` ·
  `building` · `building-1` · `tower` · `rest-house` · `room` · `hotel`
- Commercial  -  `showroom-1` · `office-space` · `warehouse` · `repair-shop` · `station` ·
  `commercial-rest-house`. Reach these by pairing `category` with `property_type=commercial`.

**Two names are not what you would guess.** Townhouses and villas share one slug,
`villa-townhouse`, and showrooms are `showroom-1` with the numeric suffix. The property-type
taxonomy at `/taxonomy` spells four of these differently, so those spellings are accepted and
normalised for you rather than quietly matching nothing: `villa` → `villa-townhouse`,
`showroom` → `showroom-1`, and `residential-building` / `commercial-building` → `building`
(listings use one merged building slug). The remaining `/taxonomy` spellings are accepted as
written; they select any listing carrying them.

not category-scoped  -  never quote it as a category total  -  and a page may return fewer rows,
or none, while later pages still match. Page until `hasMore` is `false` rather than stopping
on a short page.

Every returned listing carries its own `category`, so you can always verify the cut.

description: Search property-auction events  -  judicial (Infath) and private brokerage  -  by status, format and city.

parameters.name: seller
parameters.description:
**Which auction plane to search.** Optional  -  default `all`.

- `all`  -  every auction event
- `au-infath`  -  Infath events only. Infath is the Saudi Ministry of Justice
  enforcement-auction programme, so these are court-ordered/judicial sales
- `au-wasalt`  -  private brokerage events run on the platform itself

The distinction matters commercially: Infath lots are distressed/enforcement inventory with
a different pricing dynamic from private-brokerage events. Every result also carries its own
`sellerSlug` so you can split a mixed `all` response after the fact.

**`sellerSlug` on a result is not the value you send back here.** The private-brokerage plane
answers to `seller=au-wasalt` but its rows report `sellerSlug: "au-wasalt-group"`, and sending
that back is rejected with a 400. Split on `sellerSlug`, filter with the three values above.
The sibling `seller` field is the platform's display label and is not a stable key at all  -  it
is a slug on most slices and the Arabic name (`وصلت`) on the `format=offline` rows.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
**Page number, 1-indexed.** Optional  -  default `1`, maximum `60`.

**10 results per page, fixed**  -  there is no page-size parameter; page 2 returns
results 11 - 20. Consecutive pages are disjoint, so paging never
repeats a result.

**`estimatedCount` is exact on this plane, and `hasMore` is derived from it.** A full walk of
any slice returns the number of distinct events the count claims, so paging until `hasMore` is
`false` and paging until you have seen `estimatedCount` rows agree here  -  unlike the sale/rent
catalogue, where the count over-reports on narrow slices.

**Do not stop on a short page.** This list has genuinely short pages in the MIDDLE of it, so
"the page came back short" is not the end of the list and treating it as one drops events off
the tail. `hasMore` accounts for this; a fullness test would not.

description: Every asset under the hammer in one auction event  -  the step that turns a group id into lot ids.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description:
**Auction group id  -  one auction event, whose lots this returns.** Required.

- `1012`  -  a 13-lot event

Get one from `/auction-search` (`auctionGroups[].groupId`). Note the two-level model: an
auction **group** is the event (its schedule, deposit and brokerage), while an auction **lot**
is one asset being sold inside it. This route takes the group id and returns the lot ids;
`/auction-details` and `/auction-activity` take a lot id (`lots[].auctionId`) from the result.

An id that is not an auction group returns a clean 404.

description: Public activity feed for an auction event or a single lot  -  bids, alerts, followers.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description:
**Auction group id  -  scope the feed to a whole auction event.** Optional, but supply this
or `auction_id`: a call with neither scope is rejected as invalid rather than returning a
global feed.

- `1017`  -  an Asir auction event id, useful for testing group-scoped queries

Scoping by group returns the merged feed for **every lot in the event**, which is what you
want for an event-level watch: each entry still carries its own `auctionId`, so you can
group the feed by lot yourself. Ids come from `/auction-search` (`auctionGroups[].groupId`).
**`group_id` wins if you send both**  -  it does not narrow to one lot inside the event, it
returns the whole event feed, so send `auction_id` alone for a single-lot view.

- `100`  -  the whole first window, the default
- `20`  -  a short preview, cheaper to render

A busy live event can accumulate hundreds of entries. The feed is windowed, so read
`hasMore` and `nextCursor` on the response and pass the cursor back to walk the rest  - 
`limit` sets the window size, it does not raise a total ceiling.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
**Continuation token for the next window of the feed.** Optional  -  omit for the first page.

Take the `nextCursor` value from a response where `hasMore` is `true` and send it back here
unchanged, keeping the same `group_id` / `auction_id` scope. The token encodes the position
of the last entry returned, so entries are never repeated or skipped between windows even
while new bids land on a live event. When `hasMore` is `false`, `nextCursor` is `null` and
you have the complete feed.

group_id.description:
**Auction group id  -  scope the feed to a whole auction event.** Optional, but supply this
or `auction_id`: a call with neither scope is rejected as invalid rather than returning a
global feed.

- `1017`  -  an Asir auction event id, useful for testing group-scoped queries

Scoping by group returns the merged feed for **every lot in the event**, which is what you
want for an event-level watch: each entry still carries its own `auctionId`, so you can
group the feed by lot yourself. Ids come from `/auction-search` (`auctionGroups[].groupId`).
**`group_id` wins if you send both**  -  it does not narrow to one lot inside the event, it
returns the whole event feed, so send `auction_id` alone for a single-lot view.

auction_id.description:
**Auction lot id  -  scope the feed to a single asset.** Optional, but supply this or
`group_id`: a call with neither scope is rejected as invalid rather than returning a global
feed.

- `4882`  -  a lot inside event `1017`, useful for testing single-lot scoping; a lot's own
  feed can be empty even while its parent event carries activity, since some entries are
  recorded at the event level only

This is the per-asset view: only bids, alerts and follows against that one lot. Ids come from
`/auction-lots` (`lots[].auctionId`)  -  a **group** id sent here is a different namespace and
returns an empty feed with zero counts, not an error, so check you have the right one if a
busy event looks silent. Send it **without** `group_id`: when both are present the group
scope wins and you get the whole event feed back.

description: Auction-side vocabularies  -  lifecycle stages and seller planes  -  with stable ids.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description:
**Which auction vocabularies to return.** Optional  -  default `auction_status,auction_seller`,
which is both of them and costs no more than asking for one. Comma-separated, order-insensitive.

- `auction_status`  -  the three lifecycle stages: `auction-live` (572), `auction-upcoming` (573),
  `auction-past` (574)
- `auction_seller`  -  the two seller planes: `au-infath` (665, the Ministry of Justice enforcement
  programme) and `au-wasalt` (666, private brokerage events)

Each key you request becomes a key in the response, so a two-key request returns a two-key object
and the shape is predictable. An unknown key is rejected with a 400 naming the valid values rather
than quietly returning an empty list you might mistake for "this vocabulary is empty today".

description: The platform's own property-type and requirement vocabularies with stable ids and slugs.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description:
**Which vocabularies to return.** Optional. Comma-separated; ask for several in one call.
Omit it for the three that drive the catalogue filters  -  `property_main_type`,
`requirement_property_type_residential` and `requirement_property_type_commercial`.

Accepted keys, with what each one holds:

- `property_main_type`  -  the two top-level uses: `residential` (id 1), `commercial` (id 2)
- `requirement_property_type_residential`  -  11 home types: `apartment` 401, `villa` 402,
  `palace` 403, `residential-land` 404, `residential-building` 405, `farm` 406, `chalet` 407,
  `duplex` 408, `rest-house` 409, `floor` 417, `residential-complex` 846
- `requirement_property_type_commercial`  -  5 types: `office-space` 411, `commercial-building`
  414, `showroom` 415, `commercial-land` 416, `commercial-complex` 847
- `requirement_rental_tenure`  -  `short-term` 805, `long-term` 806
- `requirement_purchase_type`  -  how a buyer pays: `req-cash` 421, `req-mortgage` 422,
  `req-pre-approved-mortgage` 423, `req-barter` 850
- `requirement_listing_type`  -  `req-buy` 419, `req-rent` 420
- `requirement_completion_status`  -  `ready` 809, `off-plan` 810
- `requirement_timeframe`  -  buyer urgency, 6 bands from `req-immediately` 440 to
  `req-12-plus-months` 444 and `req-no-time-frame` 445
- `requirement_commercial_sub_type`  -  a thin one-entry list (`inside-mall` 672); ask for it
  only if you are mirroring the platform's own forms

Keys are matched case-insensitively and surrounding spaces are trimmed. Anything outside the
list above is rejected with a 400, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently returning one
vocabulary short. Omit the parameter  -  or send it empty  -  to get the three default
vocabularies (`property_main_type` and the two `requirement_property_type_*` lists).
